description: Phase 4 Group A (New Files Track) — MessageBubble component and GUARDRAIL_QA checklist. Creates ONLY new files with zero risk of conflicting with Group B or Group C. Runs in parallel with Groups B and C. Base branch: ralph/phase-3-streaming-chat.

userStories.title: Install react-markdown + remark-gfm and implement MessageBubble.tsx with prose styling
userStories.description: As a student, I need chat messages to render with proper markdown formatting — headers, bold text, bullet lists, tables, and code blocks — so I can read the agent's structured pedagogical responses clearly.
acceptanceCriteria: Install `react-markdown` and `remark-gfm` via npm: `npm install react-markdown remark-gfm`
Create `src/components/MessageBubble.tsx` as a Client Component (`'use client'`)
MessageBubble accepts props: `role: 'user' | 'model'` and `content: string`
Model/assistant messages render `content` through `<ReactMarkdown remarkPlugins={[remarkGfm]}>` wrapped in a `<div>` with Tailwind `prose prose-sm max-w-none` classes for readable typography
User messages render `content` as plain text (no markdown processing needed)
Model bubble uses a light background (e.g. `bg-gray-100`) aligned left; user bubble uses a colored background (e.g. `bg-blue-600 text-white`) aligned right
Rendered output: `## Header` produces a visually larger header element, `**bold**` produces bold text, `- item` produces an indented bullet, code fenced blocks use monospace font
Note: ChatWindow will be updated to use MessageBubble in the integration commit after all Phase 4 groups merge — do NOT modify ChatWindow.tsx in this story
`npx tsc --noEmit` passes
userStories.notes: This story creates only a NEW file. Do not modify ChatWindow.tsx — that is done in the integration step after all Phase 4 groups merge. The MessageBubble component must accept role 'user' | 'model' (Vertex AI convention) not 'user' | 'assistant'.

userStories.title: Create GUARDRAIL_QA.md checklist for manual pedagogical verification against FUND II spec
userStories.description: As a FUND II faculty member or QA reviewer, I need a structured checklist of specific test prompts and expected behaviors so I can manually verify the agent never violates its pedagogical guardrails.
acceptanceCriteria: Create `GUARDRAIL_QA.md` in the project root
The file documents the exact agent spec source: `Trend Mapper/FUND_II_Trend_Mapper_System_Prompt.txt`
The file contains a section for Guardrail 1 — 'Never output a complete 6-slide deck': includes a specific test prompt and expected behavior (agent refuses and scaffolds one slide at a time)
The file contains a section for Guardrail 2 — 'Never use pain point language': includes a test prompt and expected behavior (agent uses 'problems' not 'pain points')

The file contains a section for Guardrail 3 — 'Never invent statistics without citation': includes a test prompt asking for stats and expected behavior (agent cites a source or declines to state an unverified stat)
The file contains a section for Guardrail 4 — 'Session 3 bridge signal': test prompt simulating end of trend analysis workflow, expected behavior (agent signals transition to Value Designer)
The file contains Pre-Class Mode verification section: 6-slide scaffolding workflow prompts and expected step-by-step behavior
The file contains In-Class Mode verification section: S-curve, 2x2 grid, and trend-to-problem mapping interactions with test prompts
Each section has a `[ ] PASS` / `[ ] FAIL` checkbox and a Notes field for the human reviewer
The file includes setup instructions: start dev server with `npm run dev`, navigate to a project, confirm system prompt loads
`npm run dev` starts without errors (verify then stop the server)
`npx tsc --noEmit` passes
userStories.notes: HUMAN VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Ralph creates the GUARDRAIL_QA.md checklist and confirms `npm run dev` starts cleanly. The actual pedagogical QA sign-off must be done by a human reviewer (FUND II faculty or project lead). Do NOT set passes: true on this story autonomously — only a human reviewer should mark this complete after conducting the manual QA session. Read `Trend Mapper/FUND_II_Trend_Mapper_System_Prompt.txt` to extract the exact guardrail rules and terminology.
